title: The Sacred Laws of the Âryas, Part I: Âpastamba and Gautama
altTitles: Sacred Laws of the Aryas I
Sacred Books of the East, vol. 2
attributionNote: The sutras are ascribed to the sages Apastamba and Gautama and belong to their respective Vedic schools. They are cumulative school texts rather than the work of a single hand, and the surviving recensions are later than the names they carry.
description: The two oldest surviving dharmasutras set out the whole of the twice-born householder's duty: the stages of life and the student's discipline, marriage and the rules of inheritance, the daily oblations and the ancestral rites, purity and food, the law of kings and witnesses, and the penances by which offences are expiated. Apastamba's sutras are the longer and more systematic; Gautama's are terser and often older in substance.
historicalContext: The Dharmasutras are the prose forerunners of the metrical law books such as Manu, and they preserve the ritual and legal teaching of the Vedic schools of Apastamba and Gautama. Georg Bühler translated both for the Sacred Books of the East in 1879, with an introduction on the place of the texts in Indian law.
availabilityNote: Complete. Apastamba's and Gautama's law sutras with Bühler's introductions and notes are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one printed chapter per chapter. The volume's title page, contents and index are not part of the work.
